 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Subodh Abhyankar

 Shivam Soni
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Parv Birla - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Romil Verma - G.A. for the State.
 Shri Rohan Malviya - Advocate for the respondent [Obj].

Order 
1.

This is applicant's first application under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973) for grant of anticipatory bail, as he/she is apprehending his/her arrest in connection with Crime No.721/2025 registered at Police Station Hiranagar, Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Section 316(5), 318(4) and 61(2) of Bhartiya Nyay Sanhita, 2023.
2. Allegations against the applicant is of his involvement in the aforesaid case of fraud wherein the gold of worth Rs.40 lakhs was misappropriated by the accused persons.

3. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the co-accused persons namely Gopal and Bhagwan Singh have already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.59223/2025 dated 19/12/2025 on the basis of a compromise which has been entered into between the said accused persons with the complainant Surjeet Singh as both the accused persons have given a sum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:120 2 MCRC-59703-2025 Rs.47 lakhs to the complainant.

Counsel has submitted that the applicant had received a sum of Rs.40 lakhs from the complainant through Gopal and Bhagwan Singh for sale of gold and 396.27 gram gold was also delivered to co-accused Gopal, who was supposed the deliver the said gold to the complainant,

sentences.text: 1 however, it appears that Gopal did not deliver the gold to the complainant and misappropriated the same, however, admittedly, Gopal and Bhagwan Singh have already compromised the matter by paying Rs.47 lakhs to the complainant, and in such circumstances, the custodial interrogation of the applicant would not be necessary.
Counsel has also submitted that there was no reason for the co-accused persons to pay Rs.47 lakhs to the complainant if they were not guilty.

It is also submitted that the applicant is a Jeweller and the entire amount received by him was through RTGS, and have duly delivered the gold to the other accused persons Gopal and Bhagwan Singh, who were involved in the transaction.
It is also submitted that one more case under Section 420 of IPC was registered against the applicant, in which, he has already been acquitted.
Thus, it is submitted that the application be allowed.

4. Counsel for the respondent / State as also the objector, on the other hand, have opposed the prayer and it is submitted that looking to the fact that huge sum of Rs.47 lakhs is involved, no case for anticipatory bail is made out as the applicant has not delivered the gold to the complainant after he received the amount from him.

5. On due consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the case diary, it is found that there is a receipt of gold endorsed by the co-accused Gopal wherein he has been delivered the gold worth Rs.40 lakhs through the present applicant's firm G.M. Jewellers.

In such circumstances, when there is no allegation against him by co-accused Gopal that the applicant had not delivered the gold to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:120 3 MCRC-59703-2025 him and the fact that the aforesaid receipt is also available in the case diary, this Court finds that under the facts and circumstances of the case, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary in the present case.
In view of the same, applicant has made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.
6. Accordingly, this application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his/her executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
7.
The applicant shall make himself/herself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He/she shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
